Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’m using the workspace’s `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill because this task changes a multi-wake dogfish target policy. I’ll first read `README.md` and the full skill instructions, then inspect the required rollout evidence before touching `solver/` or the two documentation files.

The assigned guidance shows the sampled lineage has converged on one finite but still failing topology: a genuine upstream closing leg followed by a nose-up return and upper-boundary exit. I’m now checking whether the four sampled candidates are actually distinct, then I’ll compare their released keyframes and the inherited worker logs so the new mechanism is a controlled structural change rather than another parameter interpolation.

The visual/metric cross-check is decisive: the best partial-unload rollout is self-propelled upstream (`-0.0708` mean x velocity versus `-0.0494` local flow) but never reaches the wake corridor; the sampled posterior boost to `0.75` reproduces the same nose-up exit and slightly worsens navigation without changing posterior extrema or loads. Following the visual-first skill, I’m recording that diagnosis and a falsifiable strict-gate turn-damping hypothesis before editing the policy.

The single candidate is now implemented: it preserves the replicated `0.10/0.65` allocation and applies an additional `0.04` turn-rate damping only under the existing deep-rearward dual-opening gate. The durable guidance now closes the terminal-allocation bracket using both inherited attenuation results and the sampled `0.75` posterior-boost failure. I’m moving to the mandated runner and static contract checks; no CFD will be run.

The first mandated check exposed a rendered-workspace defect: `README.md` marks the same assigned guidance parent twice, so the checker cannot resolve a unique parent. This exact duplication is also documented in inherited worker logs. I’m removing only the redundant marker, then rerunning the guidance check.

The mandated guidance and solver-boundary checks now pass. The lightweight Julia contract command was invoked as required but cannot run because this workspace has no `julia` executable; I’m compensating with the deterministic parameter-schema/prohibited-signal audit and a final line-by-line diff review.

Produced exactly one multi-wake candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:19) adds terminal-gated turn-rate damping while preserving the sampled closing leg.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) records the visual-first diagnosis and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:126) now brackets terminal joint-allocation tuning as a negative direction.

Checks: guidance PASS, solver boundary PASS, parameter schema PASS (23/23), prohibited-signal audit PASS. Julia was unavailable, so the runtime smoke could not execute. No CFD was run.
